page: Amazon Web Services c8id.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 48 vCPUs, corresponding to 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The CPU architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It also includes 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong performance across multiple domains. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2200.0 and a multi-core score of 19875.0, with top-tier performance in image processing (20329.0) and text processing (2851.0). Memory bandwidth tests indicate strong read-only speeds, reaching 3859.38 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 194.95 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write speeds are average at 81.68 GB/sec. CPU-intensive tasks like bzip3 decompression reached 340.83 GB/sec in multi-threaded tests. For database and key-value store operations, the instance demonstrated strong capabilities, processing 86.36 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 24113.72 in PassMark database operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8id.12xlarge offers a high density of compute resources and fast local NVMe storage, making it suitable for workloads that require high CPU throughput alongside low-latency local disk access. However, the 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU represents a potential tradeoff for memory-bound applications, as the memory capacity is relatively low compared to the compute power. This hardware profile is appropriate for workloads such as software compilation, image and text processing, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from local SSD storage. It also supports moderate LLM inference, processing 254.3 tokens per second for medium (7B) model prompts, though text generation for large (70B) models is limited to an average speed of 3.16 tokens per second.
